rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection the split sky turns red like a rose-colored horse, whose coat shifts from red in winter to yellow in spring and dusty in severe cold.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة إذا تصدعت السماء وانفك بعضها من بعض

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view compares the reddened sky to the rose flower, whose colors vary but are predominantly red.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به وردة النبات وهي حمراء وقد تختلف ألوانها ولكن الأغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duhān is explained as oil, or its layered colors, when the affair reaches its end; the sky's shifting colors are compared to it.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع الدهن عند انقضاء الأمر وتناهي المدة قال الحسن هي كالدهان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan pictures the sky as oil poured in successive layers, showing different colors.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن هي كالدهان التي يصب بعضها على بعض بألوان مختلفة.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ compares the sky's changing color to a rose-colored horse, and the horse's color variation to differently colored oil; Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Qatada agree.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: شبه تلون السماء بتلون الوردة من الخيل وشبه الوردة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says duhan means red leather, whose plural is adhinah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الدهان الأديم الأحمر وجمعه أدهنة عن الكلبي.

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رياح
rows.claim: ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah explains duhan as oil sediment that takes on varied colors.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عكر الزيت يتلون ألوانا عن عطاء بن أبي رياح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing in announcing the sky's splitting is the warning and fright this information gives people in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وجه النعمة في انشقاق السماء حتى وقع التقرير بها هو ما في الإخبار به من الزجر

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that particular scene, criminals are not questioned because bewilderment overwhelms them; questioning occurs at another time, as 37:24 shows.
rows.anchor: أي لا يسأل المجرم عن جرمه في ذلك الموطن لما يلحقه من الذهول الذي تحار له العقول

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: They are not questioned to discover their deeds, since God has recorded them; rather, questioning is for rebuke and accounting.
rows.anchor: سؤال استفهام ليعرف ذلك بالمسالة من جهته لأن الله تعالى قد أحصى الأعمال

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Since people of Paradise and Hell are recognizable by their faces, they need not be asked which group they belong to; their deeds are questioned in rebuke.
rows.anchor: إن أهل الجنة حسان الوجوه وأهل النار سود الوجوه فلا يسألون من أي الحزبين هم

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida says a person who believed the truth, sinned, and did not repent is punished in the barzakh, then arrives on Resurrection Day with no sin to be asked about.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الرضا ع أنه قال: فيومئذ لا يسأل منكم عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify the criminals' marks as black faces and blue eyes.
rows.anchor: أي بعلامتهم وهي سواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون عن الحسن وقتادة.

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the marks to be signs of disgrace.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة. وقيل: بإمارات الخزي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say guards bind criminals' forelocks and feet together, drag them, and cast them into the Fire.
rows.anchor: فتأخذهم الزبانية فتجمع بين نواصيهم وأقدامهم بالغل ثم يسحبون في النار ويقذفون فيها عن الحسن وقتادة.

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another account says the guards seize them by forelocks and feet and drive them toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تأخذهم الزبانية بنواصيهم وبأقدامهم فتسوقهم إلى النار

words: هذه جهنم التي يكذب بها المجرمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shows the Hell that unbelievers denied, removing their doubts before they enter it.
rows.anchor: الكافرون في الدنيا قد أظهرها الله تعالى حتى زالت الشكوك فأدخلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God addresses the Prophet about his people: those who deny Hell will encounter it, so he should not be troubled by their case.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أنه لما أخبر الله سبحانه أنهم يؤخذون بالنواصي والأقدام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In an irregular reading, al-Hasan, al-Thaqafi, and Abu Haywa read khafidatan rafiʿatan in the accusative.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة الحسن والثقفي وأبي حيوة خافضة رافعة بالنصب.

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni parses the accusative as a circumstantial phrase; the preceding clause is another circumstantial phrase, making three permissible successive states.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني وقوله: { ليس لوقعتها كاذبة } حال أخرى قبلها أي إذا وقعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kādhiba is a verbal noun, like ʿāfiya and ʿāqiba.
rows.anchor: الكاذبة مصدر مثل العافية والعاقبة والرج التحريك باضطراب واهتزاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajj means motion with shaking and vibration, like an arrow shuddering as it leaves the bow.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم ارتج السهم عند خروجه من القوس والبس الفت كما يبس السويق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bass means kneading or mixing; the line about kneading bread witnesses the sense, and basis names meal made into travel provisions.
rows.anchor: والبس الفت كما يبس السويق أي يلت قال الشاعر: لا تخبزا خبزا وبسا بسا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows bass to mean driving, citing a line about driving snakes from a sandy hill.
rows.anchor: وبست أيضا سيقت عن الزجاج قال الشاعر: وأنبس حيات الكثيب الأهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habāʾ is fine dust visible in a sunbeam; inbithāth is the scattering of many particles in different directions.
rows.anchor: والهباء غبار كالشعاع في الرقة وكثيرا ما يخرج مع شعاع الشمس من الكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azواج means classes or kinds, as matching shoes are called a pair.
rows.anchor: والأزواج الأصناف التي بعضها مع بعض كما يقال للخفين زوجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thalātha means a group; thullah also means a portion or group of people.
rows.anchor: والثلاثة الجماعة وأصله القطعة من قولهم ثل عرشه إذا قطع ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawḍūna means interwoven like armor links; al-Aʿsha's line about David's woven mail supports the sense, as does a camel's woven girth.
rows.anchor: والموضوئة المنسوجة المتداخلة كصفة الدرع المضاعفة قال الأعشى: ومن نسج داود موضوونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idhā can be governed by the implied verbal meaning of laysa, since the intended sense is that the event's occurrence has no falsehood; another implied governor is also possible.
rows.anchor: إذا وقعت الواقعة ظرف من معنى ليس لأن التقدير لا يكون لوقعتها كاذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an omitted governor follows from context: when the event occurs, believers win and unbelievers lose.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون العامل في إذا محذوفا لدلالة الموضع عليه كأنه قال: إذا وقعت الواقعة كذلك فاز المؤمنون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali supplies an omitted subject, 'it is lowering and raising'; the phrase answers idhā by saying the event lowers some and raises others.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: تقديره فهي خافضة رافعة فأضمر المبتدأ مع الفاء وجعلها جواب إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the earth shaking may be an appositional substitute for the first idhā, an adverb attached to yaqaʿ, or a predicate of the first idhā.
rows.anchor: وقوله { إذا رجت الأرض رجا } بدل من قوله { إذا وقعت الواقعة } ويجوز أن يكون ظرفا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni allows idhā to leave its ordinary adverbial function and begins to cite Labid's line as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: ويجوز أن يفارق إذا الظرفية كقول لبيد:

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan analyzes the idhā in the cited Qur'anic phrase as genitive after hatta, so it is not adverbial.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك [يونس: 22] فإذا مجرورة عند أبي الحسن بحتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that analysis both idhā clauses are nominative, as subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: وأقول فعلى هذا لا يكون قوله إذا ظرفا في الموضعين بل كل واحد منهما في موضع الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as a grave error a contemporary grammarian's claim that Ibn Jinni made idhā rajjat govern idhā waqaʿat.
rows.anchor: بخلاف ما ظنه بعض المجودين من محققي زماننا في النحو فإنه قال: قال عثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣḥāb al-maymana is a subject with an omitted predicate such as 'what are they?'; the construction magnifies their state.
rows.anchor: فأصحاب الميمنة رفع بالابتداء والتقدير فأصحاب الميمنة ما هم أي أي شيء هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣḥāb al-mashʾama is likewise a subject with an omitted predicate, in an exclamatory construction.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب المشئمة أي أي شيء هم وهذه اللفظة مجراة مجرى التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutakiʾīn and mutaqābilīn are accusative circumstantial phrases.
rows.anchor: ومتكئين ومتقابلين نصب على الحال.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is the Resurrection, also called al-Āzifa; it is the final trumpet blast that starts the Hour.
rows.anchor: أي إذا قامت القيامة عن ابن عباس والواقعة اسم القيامة كالآزفة وغيرها

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: It is called al-Wāqiʿa because many severe events occur then, or because its impact is exceptionally severe; the phrase urges preparation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سميت بها لكثرة ما يقع فيها من الشدة أو لشدة وقعها وتقديره اذكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its arrival and manifestation are true, with no falsehood in the event, its report, or its occurrence.
rows.anchor: أي ليس لمجيئها وظهورها كذب ومعناه أنها تقع صدقا وحقا فليس فيها

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another explanation is that no false case can be made about its occurrence, established by transmitted evidence and reason.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ليس لوقوعها قضية كاذبة أي ثبت وقوعها بالسمع والعقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The event lowers some people and raises others.
rows.anchor: أي تخفض ناسا وترفع آخرين عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Jubbaʾi say it lowers some into Hell and raises others into Paradise, humbling the worldly powerful and honoring the worldly lowly.
rows.anchor: تخفض أقواما إلى النار وترفع أقواما إلى الجنة عن الحسن والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is shaken with violent motion.
rows.anchor: أي حركت حركة شديدة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid describe a severe earthquake that shakes the earth, killing those alive on its surface.
rows.anchor: زلزلت زلزالا شديدا عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد أي رجفت بإماتة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Alternatively, the earth shakes what is inside it as a sieve shakes its contents, bringing out the dead buried in it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه رجت بما فيها كما يرج الغربال بما فيه فيكون المراد ترج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Muqatil say the mountains are pulverized.
rows.anchor: أي فتت فتا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, explains the mountains as broken apart.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه كسرت كسرا عن السدي عن سعيد بن المسيب.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the mountains are uprooted from their foundations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قلعت من أصلها عن الحسن.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the mountains are moved from the earth's surface.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سيرت عن وجه الأرض تسييرا عن الكلبي.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the mountains are spread like sand and dust.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بسطت بسطا كالرمل والتراب عن ابن عطية.

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says once-towering mountains become piles of soft, shifting sand.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جعلت كثيبا مهيلا بعد أن كانت شامخة طويلة عن ابن كيسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains become scattered dust like fine motes visible in a sunbeam entering through an opening.
rows.anchor: أي غبارا متفرقا كالذي يرى في شعاع الشمس إذا دخل من الكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People become three classes, which the following verses then identify.
rows.anchor: أي أصنافا ثلاثة ثم فسرها فقال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The people of the right are those given their books in their right hands, according to al-Dahhak and al-Jubbaʾi.
rows.anchor: يعني اليمين وهم الذين يعطون كتبهم بأيمانهم عن الضحاك والجبائي.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another view says they are led rightward to Paradise or are blessed through obedience and rewarded by God; al-Hasan and al-Rabiʿ call them followers of goodness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم الذين يؤخذ بهم ذات اليمين إلى الجنة. وقيل: هم أصحاب اليمن والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'what are the people of the right?' is an exclamation magnifying their state.
rows.anchor: ثم عجب سبحانه رسوله من حالهم تفخيما لشأنهم فقال { ما أصحاب الميمنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the left receive their books in their left hands, are led leftward to the Fire, or are wretched through disobedience.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين يعطون كتبهم بشمالهم. وقيل: هم الذين يؤخذ بهم ذات الشمال إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching exclamation magnifies the dreadful fate of the people of the left.
rows.anchor: ثم عجب سبحانه رسوله من حالهم تفخيما لشأنهم في العذاب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi identifies forerunners as those who raced to follow the prophets, became leaders of guidance, and raced to abundant reward.
rows.anchor: فهم السابقون إلى جزيل الثواب عند الله عن الجبائي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forerunners race to obey God and reach His mercy; they deserve distinction because they model good, attain the highest rank first, and precede later followers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه السابقون إلى طاعة الله وهم السابقون إلى رحمته والسابق إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second occurrence of al-sābiqūn can predicate the first, or be emphatic repetition with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون السابقون الثاني خبرا عن الأول ويجوز أن يكون الثاني تأكيدا للأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who race to obedience are brought near to God's mercy, the highest ranks, abundant reward, and honor.
rows.anchor: أي والسابقون إلى الطاعات يقربون إلى رحمة الله في أعلى المراتب وإلى جزيل ثواب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their nearness is to God's honor within Paradise, whose ranks differ, so no one imagines they are brought near to another abode.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم متوهم أن التقريب يخرجهم إلى دار أخرى فأعلم سبحانه أنهم مقربون من كرامة الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil and ʿIkrima identify the forerunners as those who raced to faith.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في السابقين أنهم السابقون إلى الإيمان عن مقاتل وعكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the forerunners as those who raced to emigrate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السابقون إلى الهجرة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali identifies them as those who raced to the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى الصلوات الخمس عن علي ع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies them as those who raced to jihad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى الجهاد عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies them as those who raced to repentance and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى التوبة وأعمال البر عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they raced to everything God called them to; the author prefers this comprehensive interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى كل ما دعا الله إليه عن ابن كيسان وهذا أولى لأنه يعم الجميع

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr used to urge people, 'Advance, advance.'
rows.anchor: وكان عروة بن الزبير يقول تقدموا تقدموا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar names four forerunners: Adam's slain son, the believer from Pharaoh's people, Habib al-Najjar among Jesus' people, and Ali ibn Abi Talib among Muhammad's people.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر ع قال: السابقون أربعة ابن آدم المقتول وسابق في أمة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thullah means a numerically large group, here drawn from earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: أي هم ثلة يعني جماعة كثيرة العدد من الأولين من الأمم الماضية

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: One view says few forerunners come from Muhammad's community because its early responders are few compared with those of earlier prophets; Muqatil likewise assigns the few to this community.
rows.anchor: من أمة محمد لأن من سبق إلى إجابة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم قليل بالإضافة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view takes both groups from Muhammad's community: a large group from its earliest generations and a few from later generations whose condition resembles theirs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه جماعة من أوائل هذه الأمة وقليل من أواخرهم ممن قرب حالهم من حال أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couches are interwoven like armor links; commentators describe gold rods woven together and set with pearls and jewels.
rows.anchor: أي منسوجة كما يوضن حلق الدرع فيدخل بعضها في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recline, seated and supported like kings.
rows.anchor: أي مستندين جالسين جلوس الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They face one another, seeing faces rather than backs; this heightens joy through good company and refined manners.
rows.anchor: وذلك أعظم في باب السرور والمعنى أن بعضهم ينظر إلى وجه بعض لا ينظر في قفاه

rows.speaker: رويس
rows.claim: Ruways, transmitting from Yaʿqub, reads najmaʿukum with first-person plural nūn; the other readers use yāʾ.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ رويس عن يعقوب يوم نجمعكم بالنون والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The Medinan readers and Ibn ʿAmir read nukaffir ʿanhu and nudkhilhu with nūn in both verbs; the others read with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر نكفر عنه وندخله بالنون فيهما والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading is supported by a preceding explicit name; nūn is supported by the shift from 'He took His servant by night' to 'We gave Moses the Book' in 17:1–2.
rows.anchor: حجة الياء أن الاسم الظاهر قد تقدم ووجه النون أنه كقوله سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In dhālika bi-annahu, the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter or affair.
rows.anchor: الهاء ضمير الأمر والشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abashar is an indefinite subject licensed by the question; interrogative and negative clauses allow such subjects because they are non-assertive.
rows.anchor: أبشر مبتدأ وإنما جاز أن يكون مبتدأ مع كونه نكرة لأن الاستفهام سوغ ذلك

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Alternatively, abashar is the subject of an omitted verb explained by yahdūnanā; the verb is elided because a verb-first question is more natural.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه فاعل فعل مضمر يفسره قوله يهدوننا كأنه قال أيهدينا بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An lan yubʿathū means annahum lan yubʿathū; the clause replaces the two objects because it mentions both the report and what is reported.
rows.anchor: وقوله أن لن يبعثوا تقديره أنهم لن يبعثوا فسدت الجملة عن المفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since lan marks the future, the preceding an must be the lightened form of emphatic anna; lan prevents it from acting as a subjunctive particle.
rows.anchor: ولما كان لن في لن يبعثوا دليل الاستقبال تعينت أن قبلها لأن تكون مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm najmaʿukum is an adverb attached to tubʿathunna.
rows.anchor: يوم نجمعكم } ظرف لتبعثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nations were destroyed after messengers brought clear proofs and people rejected them as mere humans, out of contempt for following a human messenger and pride in ancestral religion.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أخلق مثلنا يهدوننا إلى الحق ويدعوننا إلى غير دين آبائنا استصغارا منهم للبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved in God, denied His messengers, and turned away from accepting them and reflecting on their signs.
rows.anchor: { فكفروا } بالله وجحدوا رسله { وتولوا } أي أعرضوا عن القبول منهم والتفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no obedience from His servants; He obligated them for their own benefit, not from need for their worship.
rows.anchor: بسلطانه عن طاعة عباده وإنما كلفهم لنفعهم لا لحاجة منه إلى عبادتهم

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the proof and clarification God showed them made any further call to guidance unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه واستغنى الله بما أظهره لهم من البرهان وأوضحه من البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of people's deeds and worthy of their praise for His blessings; alternatively, He is praised in all His acts because they are wholly beneficent.
rows.anchor: أي غني عن أعمالكم مستحمد إليكم بما ينعم به عليكم. وقيل حميد أي محمود

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar calls zaʿama a vehicle of lying; Shurayh calls it a euphemistic name for a lie.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر: زعم زاملة الكذب. وقال شريح: زعم كنية الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated reason they chose disbelief over faith was their denial of resurrection and gathering.
rows.anchor: بين الله سبحانه بعض ما لأجله اختاروا الكفر على الإيمان وهو أنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to refute them with 'Yes, by my Lord,' an oath that they will certainly be raised.
rows.anchor: فأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يكذبهم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their refutation is intensified by yes, an oath, and the emphatic lām and nūn.
rows.anchor: أكد تكذيبهم بقوله بلى وباليمين ثم أكد اليمين باللام والنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be informed of their deeds, held to account, and repaid for them.
rows.anchor: أي لتخبرن وتحاسبن بأعمالكم وتجازون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection, accounting, gathering, and requital are easy for God and involve no hardship or effort for Him.
rows.anchor: أي سهل هين لا يلحقه مشقة ولا معاناة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light sent down is the Qur'an, named for its proofs that lead to truth, like a light that guides a traveler on a road.
rows.anchor: وهو القرآن سماه نورا لما فيه من الأدلة والحجج الموصلة إلى الحق فشبه بالنور

words: أم لكم أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether God gave them enduring covenants guaranteeing their claimed good and honor until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي بل لكم عهود ومواثيق علينا عاهدناكم بها فلا ينقطع ذلك إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Baligha may mean emphatically confirmed; anything reaching completion in quality and soundness is called baligh.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالغة معناها مؤكدة وكل شيء متناه في الجودة والصحة فهو بالغ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are asked to produce a guarantor for their claim that they will receive in the next life what Muslims receive.
rows.anchor: يعني أيهم كفيل بأن لهم في الآخرة ما للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alleged partners are the idols they worship alongside God; they must bring them if their claim that they are God's partners is true.
rows.anchor: معناه أم لهم شركاء في العبادة مع الله وهي الأصنام فليأتوا بهؤلاء الشركاء

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Alternatively, the partners are witnesses who must appear on Resurrection Day to validate their claim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أم لهم شهداء يشهدون لهم بالصدق فتقوم به الحجة فليأتوا بهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the day when a terrible matter and the day's horrors become manifest.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يوم يبدو عن الأمر الشديد الفظيع عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When asked about the phrase, Ibn Abbas said obscure Qur'anic expressions should be sought in Arabic poetry, the Arabs' record; he cited a line saying war rose upon a shin to express distress.
rows.anchor: سأل ابن عباس عن قوله { يوم يكشف عن ساق } فقال: إذا خفي عليكم شيء

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains the idiom from a person exposing his shin when a grave task demands exertion; Duraid ibn al-Simma's verse illustrates it.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي: أصل هذا أن الرجل إذا وقع في أمر عظيم يحتاج إلى الجد فيه يشمر عن ساقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the day the affair becomes severe, like a situation requiring someone to roll up his clothes and expose a shin.
rows.anchor: فتأويل الآية يوم يشتد الأمر كما يشتد ما يحتاج فيه إلى أن يكشف عن ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to prostrate as a rebuke, but cannot do so.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم على وجه التوبيخ اسجدوا

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Alternatively, the day's difficulty drives them to prostrate though it can no longer benefit them, as people instinctively prostrate when frightened in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن شدة الأمر وصعوبة ذلك اليوم تدعوهم إلى السجود وإن كانوا لا ينتفعون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are lowered in humiliation and they do not lift their gaze from the ground.
rows.anchor: أي ذليلة أبصارهم لا يرفعون نظرهم عن الأرض ذلة ومهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disgrace of regret and grief overwhelms them.
rows.anchor: أي تغشاهم ذلة الندامة والحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they were healthy and able to prostrate, and were commanded to pray but did not.
rows.anchor: أي أصحاء يمكنهم السجود فلا يسجدون يعني أنهم كانوا يؤمرون بالصلاة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they heard the call 'Come to success' but did not answer it.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar swore that the verse concerns people who fail to attend congregational prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا في الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: Although paralyzed and carried between two men to the mosque, al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym refused an offered concession, saying whoever hears 'Come to success' must answer even by crawling.
rows.anchor: أنه عرض له الفالج فكان يهادى بين رجلين إلى المسجد فقيل له: يا أبا يزيد لو جلست

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abdullah describe them struck with awe, fixed stares, hearts at their throats, and regret; in life they could obey commands and avoid prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله ع أنهما قالا في هذه الآية أفحم القوم ودخلتهم الهيبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say a caller summons people to prostrate on Resurrection Day; believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs stiffen, making Muslims' prostration a source of hypocrites' regret.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة يؤذن المؤذن يوم القيامة فيسجد المؤمن وتصلب ظهور المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the backs of hypocrites become like spits or skewers.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر أنه تصير ظهور المنافقين كالسفافيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a threat: leave the deniers' affair to God and do not let it burden the Prophet, for God will handle them.
rows.anchor: هذا تهديد معناه فذرني والمكذبين أي كل أمرهم إلي كما يقول القائل دعني وإياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leads them toward punishment by degrees; the commentary refers to its earlier explanation in al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: أي سنأخذهم إلى العقاب حالا بعد حال وقد مر تفسيره في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abdullah says istidraj occurs when a servant sins, receives a fresh blessing, and then neglects to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال إذا أحدث العبد ذنبا جدد له نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God extends their lifespans without hastening punishment; only one who fears losing an opportunity rushes, while God's punishment is severe.
rows.anchor: وأطيل آجالهم ولا أبادر إلى عذابهم مبادرة من يخشى الفوت فإنما يعجل من يخاف الفوت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada explain husūman as successive days without interruption, with calamity following calamity until the people were eradicated.
rows.anchor: أي ولاء متتابعة ليست لها فترة عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say husūman means continuous or lasting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دائمة عن الكلبي ومقاتل.

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil interprets the word as cutting off: the calamity severed and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قاطعة قطعتهم قطعا حتى أهلكتهم عن الخليل.

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: ʿAtiyya reads it as ominous and unfruitful, cutting off good from its people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مشائيم نكداء قليلة الخير حسمت الخير عن أهلها عن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During those days and nights the people lay prostrate and dead.
rows.anchor: أي في تلك الأيام والليالي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they resemble decayed palm trunks.
rows.anchor: أي أصول نخل بالية عن قتادة.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains khāwiya as hollow inside.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خاوية فارغة خالية الأجواف عن السدي

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view takes khāwiya to mean fallen, like the description in 54:20.
rows.anchor:
وقيل ساقطة مثل قوله
أعجاز نخل منقعر
[القمر: 20].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāqiya is a verbal noun like ʿāfiya and ṭāghiya; the sense is whether any remnant or surviving soul remains—none survived.
rows.anchor: أي من نفس باقية من بقاء والباقية بمعنى المصدر مثل العافية والطاغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says the explanation of 'Pharaoh and those before him' has already been given.
rows.anchor: { وجاء فرعون ومن قبله } مر معناه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Muʾtafikāt are the overturned towns of Lot and, by extension, nations and communities overturned with their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي وجاء أهل القرى المؤتفكات أي المنقلبات بأهلها عن قتادة وهي قرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means their sin of associating partners with God and unbelief; as a verbal noun it resembles khaṭaʾ and khaṭīʾa.
rows.anchor: أي بخطيئتهم التي هي الشرك والكفر فالخاطئة مصدر كالخطأ والخطيئة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another explanation takes it as their wrongful deeds or as the erring person responsible for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه بالأفعال الخاطئة أي بالنفس الخاطئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nations disobeyed the messenger of their Lord in what he commanded.
rows.anchor: فيما أمرهم به وقيل: إن المراد بالرسول الرسالة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says rasūl here means the message, as in the cited poem; the plain sense, the messenger himself, is stronger.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مسلم والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the punishment as increased in severity; others say it exceeded the torment of other nations, or was high, notorious, and extraordinary.
rows.anchor: أي زائدة في الشدة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, in the Qawwas transmission, gives ʿayn in taʿīhā a partly elided vowelless pronunciation between kasra and sukūn; the others read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية القواس { وتعيها } بسكون العين مختلسا وهو بين الكسر والسكون

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read lā yakhfā with yāʾ, while the other readers use tāʾ; both readings are sound.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي لا يخفى بالياء والباقون بالتاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jāriya means a ship that sails on water and also a young woman, whose water of youth is flowing.
rows.anchor: الجارية السفينة التي من شأنها أن تجري على الماء والجارية المرأة الشابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿā means to retain knowledge; awʿaytu means to put goods into a container.
rows.anchor: يقال وعيت العلم أعيه وعيا وأوعيت المتاع جعلته في الوعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line says gathering books is useless to someone who does not preserve and retain knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال: إذا لم تكن حافظا واعيا فجمعك للكتب لا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakk means flattening; the word is related to dukān and a camel's hump spreading flat across its back.
rows.anchor: والدك البسط ومنه الدكان واندك سنام البعير إذا انفرش على ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arjāʾ means the sides or regions; its singular is rajā and dual is rajawān.
rows.anchor: والإرجاء النواحي وأحدها رجا مقصور والتثنية رجوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾum is a plural imperative meaning 'take'; the source details its forms across Hijaz, Tamim, and Qays, including forms with kāf replacing hamza.
rows.anchor: وهاؤم أمر للجماعة بمنزلة هاكم تقول للواحد هاء يا رجل وللاثنين هاؤما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hijaz, Tamim, and Qays dialects differ in forms of this imperative; some Arabs replace hamza with kāf, as in hākum, meaning 'take'.
rows.anchor: هذه لغة أهل الحجاز وتميم وقيس يقولون هاء يا رجل مثل قول أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi pauses after hāʾum and begins iqraʾū, signaling that the second verb governs the reading of the book.
rows.anchor: ووقف الكسائي على هاؤم وابتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāḍiya means pleasing or approved, an active form with passive sense because the life possesses satisfaction; the cited Nabigha line similarly uses nāṣib to mean having hardship.
rows.anchor: والراضية المرضية فاعلة بمعنى مفعول لأنها في معنى ذات رضى كما قيل لابن وتامر

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is emphatic description like 'sleeping night,' 'concealing secret,' and 'flowing water,' without ambiguity in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل ليل نائم وسر كاتم وماء دافق على وجه المبالغة في الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭūf is the plural of fruit picked; qaṭf with fatḥa names the act of picking.
rows.anchor: والقطوف جمع قطف وهو ما يقطف من الثمر والقطف بالفتح المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitābī is the object of iqraʾū because it immediately follows that verb.
rows.anchor: كتابى مفعول اقرؤوا لأنه يليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause quṭūfuhā dāniya occupies the genitive position as an adjective describing janna.
rows.anchor: جملة مجرورة الموضع لأنها صفة جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the water exceeded its known limit and flooded the earth, God carried the ancestors of the addressed people in the ship.
rows.anchor: أي جاوز الحد المعروف حتى غرقت الأرض بما عليها إلا من شاء الله نجاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd say the people carried in the ship were the ancestors of those addressed.
rows.anchor: أي حملنا آباءكم في السفينة عن ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drowning of Noah's people and rescue of those aboard is a lesson and reminder of God's blessings, inviting gratitude and reflection on His power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: لنجعل تلك الفعلة التي فعلناها من إغراق قوم نوح ونجاة من حملناه عبرة لكم وموعظة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a retaining ear is one that preserves what has come from God.
rows.anchor: أي وتحفظها أذن حافظة لما جاء من عند الله عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains it as an ear that hears and then recounts what it heard.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سامعة قايلة لما سمعت عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says every ear should retain the lesson so it admonishes those who come later.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء لتحفظها كل أذن فتكون عظة لمن يأتي بعد

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Makḥūl that when the verse was revealed the Prophet prayed, 'O God, make it Ali's ear'; Ali said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبري بإسناده عن مكحول أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Tabari's report from ʿIkrima via Burayda says the Prophet told Ali God commanded him to draw Ali near, teach him, and ensure he retained knowledge; the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: وروي بإسناده عن عكرمة عن بريدة الأسلمي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعلي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said he had asked God to make Ali the possessing ear.
rows.anchor: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب ع يقول لما نزلت
